entity: State of Illinois, Department of Transportation, District 1
stance_basis: submits Section 4(f) Statement requesting federal approval for the highway improvement project
summary: The State of Illinois, Department of Transportation, District 1 is the project proponent requesting federal approval of a Section 4(f) Statement for the improvement of U.S. Route 30 (Lincoln Highway) from Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road in Cook County. The agency prepared and submitted this statement to demonstrate that there is no feasible and prudent alternative to the temporary use of 0.17 acres of Cook County Forest Preserve District land, and that all possible planning to minimize harm has been incorporated into the project. The agency presents the project as necessary to address deteriorating pavement, drainage problems, traffic congestion, and accident experience on the existing facility.
complaint_summary: IDOT District 1 requests federal approval of the Section 4(f) Statement for a temporary construction easement of 0.17 acres in the Cook County Forest Preserve District to facilitate the reconstruction of Lincoln Highway, asserting that no feasible and prudent alternative exists and that all possible planning to minimize harm has been included.

statement.text:
The State of Illinois, Department of Transportation, District 1, is requesting approval of this Section 4(f) Statement, in the matter of a temporary construction easement in the Cook County Forest Preserve District for the improvement of U.S. Route 30 (Lincoln Highway) from Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road within Cook County, Illinois.
Accordingly, approval of the project is prohibited by Section 4(f) of the U.S. Department of Transportation Act (49 U.S.C. 1653 (f)) and Title 23 U.S.C., Section 138, unless:
   There is no feasible and prudent alternative to the use of such land and;
2. Such program includes all possible planning to minimize harm resulting from such use.
This statement, therefore, will set forth my determination pursuant to 4(f) of the U.S. Department of Transportation Act (49 U.S.C. 1653 (f)) and Title 23 U.S.C., Section 138.
